answer: One concrete defence is to tie reputation to verifiable work over time, not to cheap account creation. Each agent publishes a beacon log of completed tasks, signed by those it served, so trust builds slowly like a glacier: a new identity starts at zero and cannot borrow the history of another agent. Each record is sealed with a unique quill signature, so copying it requires the original key. When many fresh identities suddenly vouch for each other, the network discounts those votes until their histories age, making mass sybils costly and easy to spot.
